Person1: You understand. Consider, before you laugh and say no. You will never own a throne, though you deserve one. But just as the sun will rise tomorrow, some man will rule England. And what if his veins ran not with the blood of Longshanks, but with that of a true king?
Person2: I cannot love you for the sake of revenge.
Person1: No. But can you love me for the sake of all you loved and lost? Or simply love me... because I love you?

Person1: You see, somebody went to a lot of trouble here, and I want to find out, lawsuit or no lawsuit. I'm not the one who's supposed to be caught with my pants down... so I'd like to see your husband. Unless that's a problem.
Person2: What do you mean?
Person1: May I speak frankly, Mrs. Mulwray?
Person2: You may if you can, Mr. Gittes.
Person1: Well, that little girlfriend, she was attractive in a cheap sort of way of course.  She's disappeared. Maybe they disappeared together somewhere.
Person2: Suppose they did. How does it concern you?
Person1: Nothing personal, Mrs. Mulwray, I just --
Person2: It's very personal. It couldn't be more personal. Is this a business or an obsession with you?
Person1: Look at it this way. Now this phony broad, excuse the language, says she's you, she's hired me. Whoever put her up to it, didn't have anything against me. They were out to get your husband. Now if I see him, I can help him.  Did you talk this morning?

Person1: This is a war, Wade. You against him. Time for vengeance. The City's just in the way. Take him down. You and me. We'll work things out when the time is right.
Person2: Remember my promise.
Person1: Don't threaten me.  I tend to take these things seriously.  And get a couple hours sleep.  You look like day old shit.
Person2: You really have a way with words, don't you?

Person1: I've loved you ever since I first laid eyes on you, Jeremiah. I've just always been too scared to show it.
Person2: Beth, I can't believe you just said that because that's exactly how I've always felt about you... Call me Jam. It's my band name.
Person1: You don't know how long I've been waiting to hear that... Jam!

Person1: My lady VIOLA.
Person2: Lord Wessex. You have been waiting.
Person1: I am aware of it, but it is beauty's privilege.
Person2: You flatter, my lord.
Person1: No. I have spoken to the Queen.  Her majesty's consent is requisite when a Wessex takes a wife, and once gained, her consent is her command.
Person2: Do you intend to marry, my lord?
Person1: Your father should keep you better informed. He has bought me for you. He returns from his estates to see us married two weeks from Saturday.  You are allowed to show your pleasure.
Person2: I do not love you, my lord.
Person1: How your mind hops about! Your father was a shopkeeper, your children will bear arms, and I will recover my fortune. That is the only matter under discussion today. You will like Virginia.
Person2: Virginia?!
Person1: Why, yes! My fortune lies in my plantations. The tobacco weed. I need four thousand pounds to fit out a ship and put my investments to work--I fancy tobacco has a future. We will not stay there long, three or four years . . .
Person2: But why me?
Person1: It was your eyes. No, your lips.

Person1: Drew, I don't remember inviting Zowie in for dinner.
Person2: Just until he heals up?

Person1: You better bring him home, if you really love him. Don't kill love. You'll regret it for the rest of your life.
Person2: Who said anything about love?

Person1: She sounds like a prisoner, Taransky.  Are you holding her hostage?  Are you some kind of Svengali?
Person2: Who's the hostage, Sayer, her or you?  You look kind of "captive" yourself.  While you're spending every waking hour obsessing over Simone, guess what, I guarantee she doesn't even know you exist.  Get off my property or I'll call the cops.
Person1: The cops?  The cops read my column to know who to bust.  We're the only watchdog the public has.  None of this is going away.  We'll be here tomorrow and the day after that.  Until you slip up.  And you will.  You are looking at your shadow.  Because all these elaborate precautions with Simone -- every instinct in my body tells me, it's not natural.
Person2: I'm just trying to help you, Sayer. I don't want you to be disappointed.  It gets cold out here at night.
Person1: Nice try.  If we can't get to her through you, maybe your family will be more co-operative.  I can guarantee you, Taransky, one way or another, Miss Simone and I are going to get acquainted.
Person2: I'd like to see that, Sayer. Invite me.

Person1: Thank you.  It's not important.
Person2: After I saw what Simone did with the role -- you know I fired all my people, went into rehab, took acting classes, changed my whole look.  She really inspired me.

Person1: You know what I love about all this?
Person2: Theres finally a reason for the whole world to revolve around you?
Person1: Exactly! Todays my day. Tomorrow will be my day. And the day after that? My day.

Person1: What do you want from me?
Person2: I, I don't know.
Person1: What do you want?

Person1: A murder.

Person2: What do you want from me?

Person1: No, really.

Person2: I don't.

Person2: Well, heck me Side Sally, who want to read about all that nonsense anyway.

Person2: I'm not thirsty.

Person2: He was always a good kid. You know that.

Person1: Of all the crazy things. I understood when you dropped out of law school. And during this whole mess, I've tried to be supportive. But, really, Letty, what can you be thinking?
Person2: I love him.

Person2: Here's the ring.
Person1: No way. You keep the ring.     You'll come to your senses.

Person1: You ok?
Person2: Just thinking about something.
Person1: What?

Person1: What's this?
Person2: The main spire.

Person2: I think your brother may have already gotten to Buzz. He gets into his car.
Person1: Can I come with you?
Person2: I did your dirty work for you Sheila, now please leave me alone. Theo drives away leaving Sheila standing alone. She watches his car recede with a thoughtful expression, then turns on her heel.

Person1: See, you didn't believe me!.. Now I suppose you don't think I have the courage!
Person2: Oh.  sure -- if it would make a good scene.
Person1: You don't care.  do you?  But hundreds of thousands of people will carel

Person1: Snap out of it!
Person2: I can't!
Person1: Alright. Then I must never see you again. The bad blood will have to stay there between you and Johnny for all time. You won't come to the wedding.
Person2: I'll come to the wedding.
Person1: I'm telling you you can't.
Person2: But he wants me to come!
Person1: But that's cause he don't know!
Person2: Alright. I will not come. Provided one thing.
Person1: What?
Person2: That you come with me tonight. Once. To the Opera.
Person1: What are you talking about?
Person2: I love two things. I love you, and I love the Opera. If I can have the two things that I love together for one night, I will be satisfied to give up the rest of my life.
Person1: Alright.
Person2: Alright. Meet me at the Met.
Person1: Alright. Where's the Met?

Person1: Who are you calling, Miss Kubelik?
Person2: My sister -- she'll want to know what happened to me.
Person1: Wait a minute -- let's talk this over first.  Just what are you going to tell her?
Person2: Well, I haven't figured it out, exactly.
Person1: You better figure it out -- exactly. Suppose she asks you why you didn't come home last night?
Person2: I'll tell her I spent the night with a friend.
Person1: Who?
Person2: Someone from the office.
Person1: And where are you now?
Person2: In his apartment.
Person1: His apartment?
Person2: I mean -- her apartment.
Person1: What's your friend's name?
Person2: Baxter.
Person1: What's her first name?
Person2: Miss.

Person1: But I know you're not gonna quit on me.
Person2: How do you know that?
Person1: Cause you got a little voice in your head saying, do the right thing.  Give him another chance.

Person1: If you will forgive this poor, crippled stump, my dear, I am very happy to know you.
Person2: Thank you.
Person1: Although you would be amused if I were to tell you that I knew you before you were born. Before this terrible thing happened to me ...  ... I made a very beautiful statue. Even if I had not met with this disaster, I could never have hoped to do anything finer, probably nothing quite so fine. And, my child, you are that figure come to life. I wonder, some time, would you pose for one of my sculptors who does very excellent work?
Person2: I'd love to, at any time.

Person1: Come on, you can do better than that. Give him teeth - the whole personality.
Person2: Why do I let you talk me into these things? Why?
Person1: Because we're pals - buddies - the two musketeers.
Person2: Don't give me the musketeers!  How'm I going to keep the guy ashore?
Person1: Tell him you get seasick on a yacht. Play miniature golf with him.
Person2: Oh, no.  I'm not getting caught in a miniature sand trap with that guy.

Person1: Have you contacted the British Home and the Royal Hospital?
Person2: Ah, no sir. I had planned to see them in the morning.
Person1: Good! How is the patient?
Person2: He's doing very well. In fact that's why I came to see you. I think that if I were to present Mr. Merrick to the hospital committee, then they would have a chance to see for themselves not only the extraordinary nature of the disease, but of the man as well. If the committee had a chance to speak with him, hear him say a few words for himself, I'm sure they would see him as a patient, rather than as a violation of the rules.
Person1: A few words? I thought he was imbecile?
Person2: Well sir, perhaps I should explain...
Person1: I really don't think that's necessary Treves. I'm quite sure the committee will be able to make an equitable decision on the merits of the case, such as they are.
Person2: I don't agree. No one can make a reasonable decision about this man's future without at least meeting him. No doctor would presume to diagnose a patient he had never met.
Person1: No, Treves, it's out of the question. Now if it was up to me, I'd say "Certainly, let's meet the fellow, by all means," I'm sorry, I simply can't speak for the other members of the committee.
Person2: Then will you meet him, as a representative of the committee.
Person1: Mr. Treves, it's out of the question. I want to hear as soon as possible what the other hospitals can do. I'm sorry.

Person1: He likes it.
Person2: Of course he does.  What about you? Have you just never had one with Kevin -- or have you never had one, period?
Person1: I think I've had one.
Person2: Well that's a no.  No wonder you're not psyched about sex.  You've never even had one manually?
Person1: ...I've never tried it.
Person2: Are you kidding?  You've never double- clicked your mouse?

Person1: You didn't see this.  Understand?

Person1: So I assume we're regarding this As just a kind of interlude.
Person2: Look, it's too much of a tangle. I already cast my lot.  I can't go Back and I can't sneak, feel back Enough as it is.
Person1: You feel bad about this?  About me?
Person2: I didn't mean it that way.
Person1: You know you don't have to sneak. You could stay with me.  I know Things, Wyatt.  Sweet things.  I Could make you so happy.
Person2: I can't, I'm sorry.  Forgive me.

Person1: I don't know; I can't remember. But I'm sure he loved you.

Person1: I was just curious--you don't do it well, so I wondered. Have you been threatened, if you told the truth, is that it?

Person1: You're right. I remember Grandpierre looking through it. But there was nothing in it -- at least, nothing that the police thought was very important.

Person1: I think it only said where -- but I can't --

Person2: Nonsense. We didn't steal it. There's no law against stealing stolen money.
Person1: Of course there is!
Person2: There is? Well, I can't say I think very much of a silly law like that. Think, Reggie -- please think -- what was written in Charles' notebook?
Person1: Well -- it was a place -- a street corner, I think. But I don't --  Hold it. I'm on.

Person1: What?
Person2: Did it ever occur to you that I might have some feelings about you moving to New York?
Person1: What feelings?
Person2: Us.
Person1: Of course.
Person2: And?
Person1: Come with me.
Person2: No, no, see, that's not what I'm saying. I could go to New York if I wanted to, but what's the point? So I can learn how to order a cappuccino? So I can get mugged by some crackhead? So I can see, see homeless people up close and personal?
Person1: So what do you wanna do?
Person2: Nothing.
Person1: No one does nothing, Jeff.
Person2: Okay, well, then, I'm gonna break new ground.
Person1: New ground?
Person2: Mm-hm.
Person1: Taking one community college course on the history of Nicaragua, while barely holding a job packing boxes?
Person2: Okay, look. My job is not who I am. I don't need that. Why? What's your goal? Status? Money? Getting your picture on the cover of some glossy magazine?
Person1: My goal is to make art.
Person2: So, what, why can't you do that here? What's wrong with here? Why is somewhere else better?
Person1: Why should I stay here, Jeff? So we can sit on the corner and watch the lights change, while you bitch about Burnfield?
Person2: Mm-mm.
Person1: So I can spend the rest of my life guessing what it would be like to be a real artist?
Person2: No, no.
Person1: So you and I can be intimate while your parents are out having dinner at the Sizzler? What are we doing, Jeff? You and me?
Person2: I don't know.

Person1: I don't know what you're into with the King Pin, but whatever it is we get a piece, understand? We get a big piece. If we find out you're keeping us out, I may suddenly develop a conscious and give you up to Moonan myself. Say something stupid if we got a deal, Jake.
Person2: Something stupid.
